security_audit.summary: The apparent command-execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, filename formatting, JavaScript RegExp.exec, and art terminology. The only confirmed issues are intentional third-party CDN and font requests in the generated viewer template, which create low-risk supply-chain, privacy, and availability concerns.

remediation.issue: Runtime dependency on third-party CDN scripts and fonts
remediation.suggestion: Bundle p5.js and required fonts locally or document that generated artifacts contact cdnjs and Google Fonts when opened.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts encourage external script loading by default
remediation.suggestion: Pin dependencies with integrity metadata where possible, or provide an offline template variant for users with stricter security needs.

content.value_statement: Generative art can be hard to structure into reproducible, adjustable pieces. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create seeded p5.js artworks with interactive controls and clear creative rationale.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementing the artwork.
Builds browser-ready p5.js HTML artifacts from a provided viewer template.
Uses seeded randomness so the same seed reproduces the same result.
Adds parameter sliders, color controls, and seed navigation for exploration.
Guides users away from copying known artists and toward original generative systems.
Includes a JavaScript reference template for p5.js structure and utility functions.
limitations: Generated artifacts load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless modified.
The template contains placeholder algorithm sections that must be filled for final art.
It depends on browser and p5.js behavior, not server-side rendering.
It cannot guarantee artistic quality without clear direction and review.

use_cases.title: Prototype generative visuals
use_cases.description: Create a seeded p5.js sketch with controls for quick concept exploration.

use_cases.title: Teach creative coding concepts
use_cases.description: Show how randomness, noise, particles, and parameters become interactive visual systems.

use_cases.title: Prepare browser-ready art demos
use_cases.description: Generate a self-contained HTML viewer that stakeholders can open and adjust without setup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple generative sketch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first artwork.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece inspired by flowing water. Include a short philosophy and a browser-ready p5.js artifact with seed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Add adjustable parameters
prompt_templates.prompt: Create generative art based on organic growth. Add sliders for density, speed, branching, and noise scale. Make every seed reproducible.

prompt_templates.title: Design a themed interactive artifact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a specific visual direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an interactive p5.js artwork about urban night patterns. Use a subtle conceptual seed, a clear palette, and controls for motion, scale, and contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a polished exploration tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gallery-quality generative art artifact with seed navigation, reset behavior, downloadable output, and a concise explanation of the computational system.

output_examples.input: Create generative art about wind moving through tall grass.
output_examples.output: A short philosophy describing field motion, followed by an interactive browser artifact with seeded particles, wind controls, color controls, and seed navigation.

output_examples.input: Make a reproducible abstract piece with 100 variations.
output_examples.output: A seeded p5.js viewer where each seed produces a distinct variation and controls adjust density, scale, palette, and movement.

output_examples.input: Turn this theme into a polished interactive artwork for a presentation.
output_examples.output: A self-contained HTML artifact with a branded sidebar, parameter controls, reset behavior, and a concise explanation of the generative concept.

best_practices: Start with a clear visual theme and let the algorithmic philosophy guide implementation.
Use seed values and parameter controls to make results reproducible and explorable.
Review the generated artifact in a browser and adjust parameters for performance and visual balance.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for copies of a living artist or copyrighted visual style.
Do not replace the provided viewer structure unless you need a different interface.
Do not rely only on random noise without rules, constraints, or composition.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates generative art concepts and interactive p5.js HTML artifacts with seeded randomness and adjustable controls.

faq.question: Can I reproduce the same image later?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeded randomness, so the same seed and parameters should recreate the same result.

faq.question: Does the output require a server?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a self-contained HTML file that opens in a browser, though it may load external CDN resources.

faq.question: Can I change colors and parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. The viewer template includes sliders, color pickers, seed navigation, and reset controls that can be customized.

faq.question: Is this only for animated art?
faq.answer: No. It can create static or animated generative systems, depending on the requested concept and performance needs.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Provide a theme, mood, subject, or constraints. The skill can turn that input into an algorithmic philosophy and artifact.
